description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for a model evaluated across a range of initial confidence values from 0.91 to 0.99. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” is linearly scaled with tick marks at 0.01 intervals. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 0.9 with major gridlines at 0.1 intervals. The blue solid line with circle markers and error bars represents “Final Accuracy,” which remains relatively stable between 0.85 and 0.90 across most of the confidence range, dipping slightly around 0.96 and peaking near 0.98. The orange dashed line with diamond markers and error bars, labeled “Δ Accuracy,” shows the change in accuracy from initial to final; it starts near 0.55 at 0.91, peaks around 0.65 at 0.92, then declines steadily to near 0.15 at 0.99. The green dash-dot line with square markers and error bars, labeled “Initial Accuracy,” begins near 0.35 at 0.91, dips to 0.25 at 0.92, rises gradually to 0.60 at 0.96, then climbs sharply to 0.85 at 0.98 before falling slightly to 0.75 at 0.99. Error bars are present for all three lines, indicating variability in measurements.
